info.title: Manifold API
info.description: Programmatic interface to a Manifold panel. Authenticate either by logging in (cookie) or with a scoped API token from Settings → Security → API Token (Bearer). Token access is limited by its admin, monitor, node-sync, or node-admin scope; treat admin tokens like the panel password.

bearerAuth.description: Scoped API token from Settings → Security → API Token. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

cookieAuth.name: manifold
cookieAuth.description: Session cookie set by POST /login. Browser-only.

Addon.description:
Addon is a program installed into the panel through its manifest: it acts with its own
API token, narrowed to the permissions it asked for, and hears events through a webhook.

AddonInstalled.description: AddonInstalled is an install's answer: the token and signing secret, shown once.

AddonManifest.description: AddonManifest is what an addon publishes about itself (addon.json).

AddonView.description: AddonView is an installed addon with its manifest.

AdminInput.description: AdminInput is what the Admins form sends; an empty password keeps the current one.

AdminView.description: AdminView is an admin account as the Admins page shows it, without its secrets.

tier.description: Tier is admin (main admin), operator or reseller; RoleId 0 is the tier's built-in role.

volumeBytes.description: A reseller's allowance: traffic per cycle, account expiry and the users it may own.

subDomains.description: SubDomains are the hosts subscription links are built on, the first for new links.

subHappAutoDetect.description: Happ client customization settings (app-management / routing / UX).

subIncyAppAutoDetect.description:
Incy client customization settings (app-management). A "" value omits
the header so the subscriber's own app setting is left alone.

subDomains.description: SubDomains are the hosts subscription links are built on, the first for new links.

subHappAutoDetect.description: Happ client customization settings (app-management / routing / UX).

subIncyAppAutoDetect.description:
Incy client customization settings (app-management). A "" value omits
the header so the subscriber's own app setting is left alone.

AmneziaWGLogs.description:
AmneziaWGLogs is what the overview's AmneziaWG log view renders: the live
per-peer activity of every running embedded interface, plus the panel's
own recent AmneziaWG lifecycle log lines that explain a peer being absent
from Peers at all.

example: 2025/01/01 12:00:00 amneziawg: started interface awg1 for inbound 1

token.description: SHA-256 hash; the plaintext is shown only once at creation

userId.description: UserId is the account the token acts as (0 is the owner); Tier and Permissions narrow it further.
Acts-as account, tier and permissions narrow an admin-scope token; empty permissions mean no restriction.

AppAccount.description:
AppAccount is the account a session belongs to, summed over its subscription.
ExpiryTime is in ms (0 never, negative counts from first use); Total 0 is unlimited.

AppConfig.description:
AppConfig is one entry of the subscription. Outbound is set when Xray can run it;
LocationID is absent when its inbound serves no location, as on an external link.

AppLocation.description:
AppLocation is a place the app offers, served by the inbounds linked to it on any
protocol or server; InboundIds is kept in AppLocationInbound.

AppPlace.description: AppPlace is a location as the app sees it, without the panel's inbound ids.

AppProfile.description: AppProfile is what GET .../app/v1/profile answers a signed-in device.

AuditEntry.description: AuditEntry records one admin action; secrets in Detail are redacted before it is stored.

AuditPage.description: AuditPage is one page of the log, newest first.

AuditSettings.description: AuditSettings is the change-logging switch and how long records are kept.

AvailabilityBar.description:
AvailabilityBar is one stretch of the availability bar: up, down (any slot unanswered) or
unwatched (the panel recorded nothing, being off or the node not yet added).

BackupFile.description: BackupFile is one certificate or key the panel's settings point at.

BackupTarget.description:
BackupTarget is where scheduled full backups go: this server, an S3 bucket or another
server over SSH. Secrets are write-only and never leave the panel.

BackupTargetInput.description: BackupTargetInput saves a target; a nil secret keeps the stored one, "" clears it.

BackupTargetView.description: BackupTargetView is a target without its secrets, saying which are set.

CatalogTheme.description:
CatalogTheme is one theme a catalogue offers. Files sit beside the catalogue in a
directory named after the theme, or in Path when it says otherwise.

Certificate.description:
Certificate is one certificate of the store, issued over ACME or uploaded, kept as PEM
files under the panel's folder and copied to the nodes it names.

CertificateInput.description: CertificateInput saves an ACME certificate's settings; a nil DNSToken keeps the stored one.

CertificateUpload.description: CertificateUpload stores a certificate made elsewhere.

CertificateView.description: CertificateView is a certificate without its secrets, with the files it is kept in.

Client.description: Client represents a client configuration for Xray inbounds with traffic limits and settings.

allowedIPsByInbound.description:
AllowedIPsByInbound optionally overrides AllowedIPs on a per-inbound
basis, keyed by inbound id. Lets one identity attached to both
WireGuard and AmneziaWG carry two genuinely different addresses in a
single Create/Update call instead of the shared AllowedIPs field
being broadcast to every attached tunnel inbound. Absent/unset for a
given inbound id falls back to the shared AllowedIPs exactly as
before -- fully backward compatible for callers that never set this.

clientHostRuleIds.description:
ClientHostRuleIds binds the client to these host rules, one link each; nil preserves, empty
clears, and bindings with no usable host leave that inbound out of the subscription.

contacts.description:
Contacts is what the panel knows about the customer, by field: telegram, email, phone,
bale, soroush and rubika are searched and exported; any other field is only kept.

forwardedPorts.description: AmneziaWG port-forwarding spec, e.g. "80,443,8000-8100"; "" withdraws the forwards, omit to keep them

keepAlive.description: Numeric values or AmneziaWG ranges; 0 disables, omission preserves.

resetDay.description: Calendar renewal day 1-31, 0 disables monthly renewal

speedLimit.description: Mbps in each direction on each host; 0 is unlimited

trafficReset.description: Per-client traffic reset cycle, independent of the inbound's own (#5497).

trafficResetMonth.description:
The month of a yearly cycle, the length of an every-N-days one, and the
calendar (gregorian or persian) monthly and yearly cycles follow.

ClientPageResponse.description:
ClientPageResponse is the shape returned by ListPaged. `Total` is the
row count in the DB; `Filtered` is the count after Search/Filter/Protocol
were applied, before pagination. The page contains at most PageSize items.
Summary is computed across the full DB row set so dashboard counters
on the clients page stay stable as the user paginates/filters.

ownerId.description: OwnerId is the admin account the user belongs to; 0 is the panel (main admins).

trafficResetMonth.description: TrafficResetMonth, TrafficResetEvery and TrafficResetCalendar shape the cycle; see Client.

ClientSlim.description:
ClientSlim is the row-shape used by the clients page. It drops fields the
table never reads (UUID, password, auth, flow, security, reverse, tgId)
so the list payload stays compact even when the panel manages thousands
of clients. Modals that need the full record still call /get/:email.

subUrl.description:
SubUrl and its JSON and Clash siblings are the user's own subscription addresses,
on its reseller's domain or its own host under a wildcard; "" when that format is off.

ClientTraffic.description:
ClientTraffic represents traffic statistics and limits for a specific client.
It tracks upload/download usage, expiry times, and online status for inbound clients.

resetCount.description: ResetCount is how many have fired, so a prepaid plan stops on its own.

resetDay.description:
ResetDay renews on that day of each calendar month instead of every
Reset days; 0 disables monthly renewal.

resetMax.description: ResetMax caps how many times auto-renew may fire; 0 means no cap.

resetWeekday.description: ResetWeekday renews weekly at panel-local midnight: 1 Monday through 7 Sunday.

ClientUsageView.description: ClientUsageView is a user's traffic over a window: slot by slot and per server.

ClientsSummary.description:
ClientsSummary collects per-bucket counts plus the matching email lists so
the clients page can render the dashboard stat cards and their hover
popovers without shipping the full client array. The counters are exact;
the lists stop at clientSummaryEmailCap entries and only back the popovers.

EngineStatus.description:
EngineStatus says whether this server can run the inbounds of a protocol
that is served outside Xray.

package.description: Package is the system package that brings the engine.

FallbackParentInfo.description:
FallbackParentInfo carries everything the frontend needs to rewrite a
child inbound's client link: where to connect (the master's address
and port) and which path matched on the master's fallbacks array.
The frontend already has the master inbound in its dbInbounds list,
so we only ship identifiers + the match path here.

GeoCategory.description: GeoCategory is one code inside a database, such as geosite's "google".

GeoCategoryPage.description: GeoCategoryPage is one page of categories plus the unpaged total.

GeoEntry.description:
GeoEntry is a single rule inside a category: a domain rule for geosite
databases, a CIDR for geoip ones.

GeoEntryPage.description: GeoEntryPage is one page of category entries plus the unpaged total.

GeoFile.description: GeoFile describes one .dat database found in the asset directory.

GeodataTokenIssue.description:
GeodataTokenIssue reports a routing token the running core would reject,
or would silently match nothing against.

HistoryOfSeeders.description: HistoryOfSeeders tracks which database seeders have been executed to prevent re-running.

finalMask.description:
FinalMask is a JSON object of xray finalmask masks (tcp/udp/quicParams),
merged into this host's JSON-subscription stream. Empty = no override.

vlessRoute.description:
Single VLESS route value (0-65535) baked into the subscription UUID's 3rd
group (bytes 6-7), which xray reads via net.PortFromBytes(id[6:8]). Empty = none.

HwidSlotStatus.description:
HwidSlotStatus is the aggregate device-slot view exposed to subscribers:
counters only, no hwid value or hash, no email, no device metadata.

ImportApplyRequest.description: ImportApplyRequest creates the users of a preview on the inbounds picked per protocol.

fallback.description: Fallback takes the users that have no credential for any picked protocol.

ImportApplyResult.description: ImportApplyResult is what an import created.

ImportPreview.description: ImportPreview is what a source holds, kept for importKeep under Id.

ImportUserPreview.description: ImportUserPreview is one user of a read source, as the preview lists it.

Inbound.description: Inbound represents an Xray inbound configuration with traffic statistics and settings.

excludeFromSub.description: Whether to omit this inbound from subscription output while keeping it operational

fallbackParent.description:
FallbackParent is populated by the API layer when this inbound is
attached as a fallback child of a VLESS/Trojan TCP-TLS master.
The frontend uses it to rewrite client-share links so they advertise
the master's externally reachable endpoint instead of the child's
loopback listen. Not persisted.

originNodeGuid.description:
OriginNodeGuid is the panelGuid of the node that physically hosts this
inbound, propagated up across hops (#4983). Empty for an inbound that
lives on this panel's own xray; set to the originating node's GUID when
the inbound was synced from a node (kept as-is across further hops). Lets
the master attribute a deeply nested inbound to the real node instead of
the intermediate one it was fetched through.

subSortIndex.description: Sort order of this inbound's links in subscription output only (lower first; negatives allowed; 0/omitted → 1; ties by id)

trafficResetDay.description: Day of month for monthly traffic resets

InboundClientIps.description: InboundClientIps stores IP addresses associated with inbound clients for access control.

awgServer.description:
AwgServer carries the full AmneziaWG server block (keys, subnet,
obfuscation params) so the clients page can render a downloadable
per-client .conf without a second round trip.

nodeAddress.description:
Share-host resolution inputs, mirroring the subscription's
resolveInboundAddress so the clients page renders a node-managed WireGuard
Endpoint that points at the node, not the master panel. NodeAddress is the
hosting node's externally reachable address (empty for this panel's own
inbounds); Listen and ShareAddrStrategy/ShareAddr feed the same
node→listen→custom fallback the share/QR links already use.

nodeId.description:
Hosting node; nil for this panel's own inbounds. Lets the clients
page map a node filter onto inbound IDs (#4997).

IngressListener.description: IngressListener shares one TCP port among services by the name each connection asks for.

defaultTarget.description: DefaultTarget takes what no route names; empty closes it.

IngressRoute.description: IngressRoute sends the TLS names or HTTP hosts in Hosts to Target.

IngressStatus.description: IngressStatus is a listener as saved, and the reason it is not serving if it is not.

defaultTarget.description: DefaultTarget takes what no route names; empty closes it.

MeView.description: MeView is the signed-in account: what it may reach and, for a reseller, its allowance.

catalogue.description: Catalogue and TierCeilings feed the role and token forms.

MigrationAddress.description: MigrationAddress is an address users' configs carry, and what a move does to it.

MigrationIssue.description: MigrationIssue is one finding of a restore check, named by code for the page to word.

MigrationReport.description: MigrationReport is what a restore would do, or did, on this server.

MigrationTunnel.description: MigrationTunnel is a tunnel of the backup and what happens to its other end.

Node.description:
Node represents a remote 3x-ui panel registered with the central panel.
The central panel polls each node's existing /panel/api/server/status
endpoint over HTTP using the per-node ApiToken to populate the runtime
status fields below.

guid.description:
Guid is the remote panel's stable self-identifier (its panelGuid),
learned from each heartbeat. It is the globally stable node identity used
to attribute online clients/inbounds to the physical node across a chain
of nodes (#4983); panel-local autoincrement ids don't survive a hop.
Observed-state only — never user-edited.

parentGuid.description:
ParentGuid + Transitive are set only when a node is surfaced as part of a
node tree (#4983): direct nodes carry the master panel's own GUID, a
transitive sub-node carries its parent node's GUID. Transitive nodes are
read-only projections (Id == 0, not persisted) — never edited or deployed.

status.description:
Heartbeat-updated fields. UpdatedAt advances on every probe even when
the row is otherwise unchanged so the UI's "last seen" tooltip is
truthful without us having to read LastHeartbeat separately.
online|offline|unknown

trafficMultiplier.description: TrafficMultiplier scales what this node's traffic costs users' quotas; 0 is read as 1.

unavailableMetrics.description: Nil on legacy rows and responses: zero remains a valid measured value.

usageLimit.description:
A cap on the node's raw traffic per period (bytes; 0 none): reaching it stops the
node's inbounds until the period turns.

xrayState.description:
XrayState and XrayError are captured from the remote node's /panel/api/server/status
during heartbeats. They let the central panel distinguish "panel API reachable"
(status=online) from "Xray core itself has failed on the node" for monitoring.

NodeHealthPoint.description: NodeHealthPoint is the node's load over one stretch of the chart.

NodeInstallJob.description: NodeInstallJob is what an install has done so far.

NodeInstallRequest.description:
NodeInstallRequest installs (or updates) Manifold on a server over SSH and adds it as a
node. SSH credentials are used for this job only and never stored.

NodeMutationRequest.description:
NodeMutationRequest is the node write/probe contract. ApiToken is accepted
only as input. On update, nil means keep the stored token; replacement and
clearing are explicit and mutually exclusive.

NodeStatsView.description: NodeStatsView is a node's health and traffic over a window.

NodeUsage.description: NodeUsage is what a user moved through one server in a window; node 0 is this panel.

NodeView.description:
NodeView is the browser/API read contract for nodes. Credentials are
write-only: responses expose only whether a node has a token configured.

OpenVPNCertInfo.description: OpenVPNCertInfo is what the OpenVPN form shows of one certificate.

OpenVPNKeySet.description: OpenVPNKeySet is a new key set for an OpenVPN inbound, for its form to save.

OutboundTraffics.description: OutboundTraffics tracks traffic statistics for Xray outbound connections.

OwnerView.description: OwnerView names an account users can belong to, for the users page's owner column and filter.

PanelSummary.description:
PanelSummary is the business side of the dashboard: users, today's traffic, nodes,
webhooks and backups.

PanelUpdateStatus.description:
PanelUpdateStatus reports the outcome of the most recently launched panel
self-update. RunID lets the caller confirm this status belongs to the
update it started rather than a stale result left over from an earlier
run; State is one of "pending", "success", or "failed". RunID is a decimal
string, not a JSON number: it's a formatted UnixNano timestamp, and
JavaScript's number type can't represent that precisely (it exceeds
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), which would let two different runs round to the
same value on the wire and defeat the whole point of this field.

PeerActivity.description:
PeerActivity is one peer's live embedded-Device-reported state, the
counterpart of an Xray access-log entry: a tunnel logs no requests, only
handshakes and bytes.

handshake.description: Handshake is unix milliseconds, 0 when the peer has never connected.

Plan.description: Plan is a preset a new user is created from; nothing links the user to it afterwards.

PortForward.description: PortForward is one port, or range, the server side exposes and sends to the client side.

xrayState.description:
XrayState/XrayError are populated on successful probes even when the node's
Xray core is not healthy. The UI uses them for a distinct "panel ok, xray failed" indicator.

Readiness.description: Readiness is the host's ability to run any kernel-mode inbound at all.

certChainBytes.description:
CertChainBytes is the sum of DER lengths of the presented peer chain.
xray-core ML-DSA-65 REALITY needs >= 3500 bytes (constant lives in xray-core).

certChainValid.description:
CertChainValid ignores the name: a trusted chain presented for other names
still has serverNames the panel can offer instead of the failing SNI.

privateTarget.description:
PrivateTarget marks a target that resolves to a loopback/private/link-local
address: blocked before the probe unless the caller opted in, then flagged.

Role.description: Role narrows one tier: the permissions it keeps and the caps on what its accounts hand out.

minUserBytes.description: Bounds on what the role's accounts hand out per user; 0 is no bound on that side.

usersReadScope.description: Which users the role reads and changes: all (empty) or its own; a reseller is always own.

ServerSettings.description:
ServerSettings is the "server" block of an AmneziaWG inbound's Settings
JSON: the interface-level configuration shared by every client/peer. The
listen port is deliberately not duplicated here — it lives on the inbound
row itself (Inbound.Port), like every other protocol.

externalInterface.description:
ExternalInterface, IPv6Enabled, and IPv6ExternalInterface are live
again as of Phase 3.5 -- see the matching fields on Instance for what
they gate (internal/amneziawgnet's IPv6-address-alias mechanism).
IPv6Subnet was never actually vestigial either: InstanceFromInbound
already consumes it (via serverAddressV6) to build the server's own
tunnel address, same as always. Only RouteThroughXray, below, remains
genuinely vestigial as of the hard cutover to the embedded path
(internal/amneziawgnet) -- read from existing stored settings for
backward compatibility, but not acted on by anything.

headerProtectionKey.description:
HeaderProtectionKey and ContentPaddingAddition are AmneziaWG 3.0
fields, flat and top-level for the same tools/openapigen reason as
the block above; Obfuscation() below folds them back into
Obfuscation31's own identically named fields.
HeaderProtectionKey is a base64 32-byte key; empty (the default)
disables AWG 3.0 header protection. A non-empty value requires
every one of S1-S4 above to be >= 12 -- ValidateObfuscation
enforces this at save time, not just at IpcSet time.
ContentPaddingAddition is a "low-high" range or bare integer, the
same grammar and uint32 cap as H1-H4.

jc.description:
Obfuscation31's fields, repeated flat (not embedded) rather than
nested under their own key: encoding/json would happily inline an
embedded Obfuscation31 the same way, but the frontend's Go->Zod/TS
generator (tools/openapigen) does not — it emits a genuinely nested
`obfuscation31` object, which would silently diverge from the real
wire JSON. See Obfuscation() below for the manager-facing conversion.

kernelMode.description:
KernelMode runs this inbound on the AmneziaWG kernel module (internal/amneziawgkern)
instead of the embedded amneziawg-go + gVisor stack.

primaryDns.description:
PrimaryDNS/SecondaryDNS seed client configs' DNS line. Blank is
meaningful, so no omitempty: a dropped key resurrects frontend defaults.

randomTrailers.description:
RandomTrailers/DisableCookies mirror Instance's identically named
AmneziaWG 3.1 fields -- see that type's own doc comment for the real
protocol/interop details. Both real bool fields (not omitempty):
buildUAPIConfig always emits both lines explicitly so the
reconfigure-in-place diff correctly notices a true->false edit, not
just false->true.

rekeyAfterTime.description:
RekeyAfterTime/RekeyTimeout/RejectAfterTime/KeepaliveTimeout/
MaxHandshakeAttempts mirror Instance's identically named fields --
see that type's own doc comment for the grammar/width/real-default
details. Flat and top-level for the same tools/openapigen reason as
the rest of this struct.

Setting.description: Setting stores key-value configuration settings for the 3x-ui panel.

SubBalancer.description:
SubBalancer is one extra JSON-subscription config document whose members are
the selected inbounds' proxy outbounds. SortOrder shares SubSortIndex semantics.

enabled.description:
No gorm default:true — a bool default makes an explicit false at insert
collapse back to the column default (zero value is skipped).

memberWeights.description:
inboundId -> leastLoad weight; absent entries mean 1.0. Only meaningful
with Strategy "leastLoad" — xray ignores costs on every other strategy.

TgBotCapabilities.description: TgBotCapabilities is the browser-safe shape of the bot's own capabilities.

groupPrivacy.description:
GroupPrivacy off means the bot reads every group message; when it is on,
a bare /start in a group is invisible to the bot.

Theme.description: Theme is one entry of the panel's theme picker.

Traffic.description:
Traffic represents network traffic statistics for Xray connections.
It tracks upload and download bytes for inbound or outbound traffic.

TunnelGroup.description:
TunnelGroup is a set of this relay's tunnels to several origins that share forwarded
ports, in failover or balance; Settings holds the forwards as tunnel settings do.

TunnelGroupView.description: TunnelGroupView is a group with the forwards it shares.

TunnelPairing.description: TunnelPairing is the code the other end of a tunnel imports.

TunnelRelay.description: TunnelRelay is a relay this panel manages over its API with a tunnel-scoped token.

version.description: Version is the relay's product version as its last answer gave it; empty until it answers.

TunnelRequest.description: TunnelRequest is what the tunnel form saves.

TunnelSettings.description: TunnelSettings is the JSON a tunnel row keeps; each kind reads the fields it needs.

dialer.description: Dialer says which role opens a layer-3 tunnel; the other one listens on Port.

localAddr.description: LocalAddr binds the outer packets to one of this server's addresses; empty lets the route choose.

port.description: Port is where the listening side of a BackPack tunnel waits for the other.

publicAddr.description: PublicAddr is how the other side reaches this server; empty means the detected public address.

remoteAddr.description: RemoteAddr is the other server's public address, or the relay's host for a reverse client.

TunnelStatus.description: TunnelStatus is what the panel shows of one tunnel end.

TunnelSuggestion.description: TunnelSuggestion is a free tunnel subnet, port and secret for a new tunnel.

TunnelView.description: TunnelView is a tunnel end as the panel shows it, with how it is doing.

TwoFactorSetupView.description: TwoFactorSetupView is a fresh secret for the account's authenticator app.

UsagePoint.description: UsagePoint is the traffic of one slot.

User.description: User represents a user account in the 3x-ui panel.

tier.description: Tier is admin (main admin), operator or reseller; RoleId 0 is the tier's built-in role.

volumeBytes.description: A reseller's allowance: traffic per cycle, account expiry and the users it may own.

UserCounts.description: UserCounts is how many users are in each state; a user can be expired and limited at once.

UserUsage.description: UserUsage is what one user moved through a server in a window.

Webhook.description: Webhook receives events: a signed HTTP POST, an ntfy topic, or a Bale bot message.

userId.description: UserId is the account the webhook belongs to; a reseller's hears only its own users.

WebhookDelivery.description: WebhookDelivery is one event owed to one webhook: the outbox row and its delivery log.

WebhookInput.description: WebhookInput saves a webhook; a nil Secret keeps the stored one.

WebhookPayload.description: WebhookPayload is the JSON body a webhook receives.

WebhookView.description: WebhookView is a webhook without its secret; Secret is filled once, when it is made.

userId.description: UserId is the account the webhook belongs to; a reseller's hears only its own users.

WireGuardImportResult.description: WireGuardImportResult says what an imported interface became.

disabled.description: Disabled counts the clients imported switched off, as WGDashboard had restricted them.

dropped.description: Dropped lists the interface settings an inbound does not carry over.

skipped.description: Skipped lists the peers left out, each with the reason.
example: old-laptop: has no address in the tunnel

withoutKey.description: WithoutKey counts the clients whose private key is unknown, so the panel cannot show their config.

WireGuardImportSources.description: WireGuardImportSources is what this server offers to import.

dashboardDb.description: DashboardDB is the WGDashboard database peer names and usage are read from, if one was found.

WireGuardImportable.description: WireGuardImportable is an interface of this server that can become an inbound.

problem.description: Problem says why the interface cannot be imported; empty when it can.

restricted.description: Restricted counts the peers WGDashboard keeps switched off for this interface.

payload.description: Shape is selected by type; see x-websocket-events on GET /ws.

time.description: Server emission time in Unix milliseconds.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Two authentication modes are supported. UI sessions use a cookie set by the login endpoint. Programmatic clients (bots, scripts, remote panels) authenticate with a Bearer token taken from Settings → Security → API Token. Both work for every endpoint under /panel/api/*.

tags.name: Inbounds
tags.description: Manage inbound configurations and their clients. All endpoints live under /panel/api/inbounds and require a logged-in session or Bearer token. Link-generating endpoints honour forwarded headers only when the request comes from a configured trusted proxy.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: System status, log retrieval, certificate generators, Xray binary management, and backup/restore. All under /panel/api/server.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Manage clients as first-class entities that can be attached to one or more inbounds. A single client row drives the settings.clients entry in every inbound it belongs to. Endpoints live under /panel/api/clients.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description: Manage remote Manifold panels acting as nodes for a central panel. All endpoints under /panel/api/nodes.

tags.name: Addons
tags.description: An addon is a program next to the panel, such as a sales bot, installed from its manifest (addon.json: id, name, version, permissions, events, webhook, panelUrl). Installing gives it an API token that acts as the installing account, narrowed to the permissions it asks for and never above that account, and a signed webhook for the events it names; both are shown once and go into the addon's own settings. Installing the same id again updates the permissions, events and webhook in place. Disabling turns the token and webhook off together; uninstalling removes them. All endpoints under /panel/api/addons.

tags.name: Import from another panel
tags.description: Moves users in from Marzban, PasarGuard, Marzneshin, 3x-ui/x-ui and s-ui (their SQLite database), Hiddify (its JSON backup), or Marzban, PasarGuard and Remnawave over their API. A read returns a preview held for 30 minutes; apply creates the users on the inbounds picked for each protocol, keeping each user's UUID or password, quota, usage, expiry and reset cycle. With keepLinks the old panel's subscription links keep working on this panel's subscription server: kept ids (3x-ui, s-ui, Hiddify, Remnawave), Marzneshin's /sub/<user>/<key>, and Marzban/PasarGuard tokens checked against the old panel's secret. Users whose name is already taken are skipped. All endpoints under /panel/api/import.

tags.name: Certificates
tags.description: The certificate store: certificates issued by the panel over ACME (Let's Encrypt; HTTP-01, TLS-ALPN-01, or DNS-01 through Cloudflare or ArvanCloud for wildcards) or uploaded, kept as fullchain.pem and privkey.pem under /etc/manifold/certs/<name>/ for inbounds and the panel to read. Renewed 30 days before expiry; a renewal restarts Xray when an inbound reads the files, the panel picks up its own certificate without a restart, and each named node gets a copy. The DNS token, account key and private key are never returned. All endpoints under /panel/api/certs.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Events sent out as they happen: to your own URL (JSON, signed), an ntfy topic, or a Bale chat. An HTTP delivery carries X-Manifold-Event, X-Manifold-Delivery (the event id, for de-duplication), X-Manifold-Timestamp and X-Manifold-Signature = sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<body>"). A delivery that does not get a 2xx is retried after 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h and 8h, then given up; the log keeps a week. A reseller sees and makes only its own webhooks, hears only about its own users, and may only reach public addresses. All endpoints under /panel/api/webhooks.

tags.name: Scheduled backups
tags.description: Targets that receive a full backup on a schedule: a directory of this server, an S3-compatible bucket (AWS, Cloudflare R2, ArvanCloud, MinIO; path-style, Signature V4) or another server over SSH. With a passphrase the backup is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a PBKDF2 key; restore asks for it. Only the newest backups the target keeps are left; other files there are never touched. Secrets (passphrase, secret key, password, private key) are write-only. All endpoints under /panel/api/backups.

tags.name: Shared ports
tags.description: One TCP port, such as 443, shared by many services: each connection goes to the target its TLS server name (SNI) or HTTP Host names, untouched, so REALITY and TLS inbounds, the panel and the subscription server can all answer on one port. Routes are tried in order; a route may also require an ALPN. A target may receive a PROXY protocol header so it sees the real client address. Runs on this server only. All endpoints under /panel/api/ingress.

tags.name: Tunnels
tags.description: Tunnels between this server and another: kernel GRE, GRETAP, IP6GRE, IP6GRETAP, IPIP and SIT links, and BackPack reverse and layer-3 tunnels. The client end runs on the panel that serves the accounts, the server end on the relay users connect to, which forwards its ports to the client end. A relay is another Manifold, usually the tunnel edition, reached with an API token of the tunnel scope. All endpoints under /panel/api/tunnels.

tags.name: Access
tags.description: Admin accounts, custom roles, plans and the audit log. Accounts sit on a tier (main admin, operator, reseller); a reseller works only on the users it owns, inside its allowance. All endpoints under /panel/api/access.

tags.name: Hosts
tags.description: Per-inbound override endpoints. Each enabled host renders one extra subscription link/proxy with its own address/port/TLS, superseding the legacy externalProxy array. All endpoints under /panel/api/hosts.

tags.name: Backup
tags.description: Operations that interact with the configured Telegram bot.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Panel configuration and user credentials. All endpoints live under /panel/api/setting and require a logged-in session or Bearer token.

tags.name: API Tokens
tags.description: Manage scoped Bearer tokens for programmatic auth. admin grants the full panel API; monitor is read-only for status and metrics; node-sync manages node configuration without panel updates; node-admin adds panel self-update to node-sync. Tokens may expire and are stored as SHA-256 hashes. The plaintext is returned only once at creation.

tags.name: Xray Settings
tags.description: Xray configuration template, outbound management, Warp/Nord/PIA integration, and config testing. All endpoints under /panel/api/xray.

tags.name: Subscription Balancers
tags.description: Client-side balancers for the JSON subscription: each enabled balancer is emitted as one extra config document whose members are the proxy outbounds of the selected inbounds (routing.balancers + burstObservatory). Managed in Settings → Sub Balancers.

tags.name: App
tags.description: The locations the app offers. A location (Germany, say) gathers the inbounds that serve it, on any protocol and any server; an inbound serves one location at most, and one in none is still used by the app's quick connect. The app itself signs in on the subscription server (see Subscription Server → app/v1); app access is switched on with the appEnable setting.

tags.name: Subscription Server
tags.description: A separate HTTP/HTTPS server that serves proxy subscription links (standard, JSON, and Clash) to clients. The server listens on its own port (default 2096) and is configured in Settings → Subscription. Fresh panels generate random path prefixes for each format; all paths remain configurable. Every subscription endpoint sets response headers for client apps to read traffic/expiry info.

post.summary: Create a new client and attach it to one or more inbounds in a single call. Body is JSON. Per-protocol secrets are generated server-side when omitted, so callers can send only the universal fields.
post.description:
Client email must not be exactly `.` or `..`. Existing reserved-name clients can be read, renamed to a valid name, or deleted using the query-parameter /get, /update and /del aliases. Fields the server fills in when they are omitted — a valid value sent by the caller is never overwritten. Re-adding an email that already exists, with its stored `subId`, reuses the stored `id`, `password`, `auth` and `secret` instead of minting new ones, so the identity stays in sync across its inbounds.

- **VLESS / VMess** — `id`, a fresh UUID
- **Trojan** — `password`
- **Shadowsocks** — `password`. On a `2022-blake3-*` inbound a supplied password that does not base64-decode to the key length of the cipher (16 or 32 bytes) is replaced by a generated key and the call still succeeds, so read the client back if you did not let the server pick. Legacy ciphers keep any non-empty password
- **Hysteria** — `auth`
- **mtproto** — `secret`, a FakeTLS secret derived from the fronting domain of the inbound, or from `www.cloudflare.com` when it has none
- **WireGuard** — `privateKey` and `publicKey` when both are blank, or `publicKey` alone when only a `privateKey` was sent, plus `allowedIPs`: one free `/32` taken from the /24 the existing peers of that inbound already sit in, or from `10.0.0.0/24` when it has none

Accepted on the same body but never generated: `preSharedKey` and `keepAlive` (WireGuard), `adTag` (mtproto).

WireGuard is the only one of these that can fail. Allocation widens the search to the containing /16 before giving up with `inbound <id>: wireguard: no free address available in <scope>`, and an `allowedIPs` supplied by the caller is validated instead of allocated: `inbound <id>: wireguard: allowedIPs entry <entry> overlaps <address> used by another client` when its range overlaps an address or prefix a different client of that same inbound holds, or `... used by a client on <inbound>` when the holder sits on another WireGuard or AmneziaWG inbound. Ranges are compared, not strings, so `10.0.0.9/24` collides with `10.0.0.5/32`; a `/0` entry collides with every address of its family another client holds, and only a `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` default route that is already stored (legacy peers) keeps nobody out. Allocation likewise skips every address inside a prefix another client holds. The same validation runs on POST /panel/api/clients/{email}/attach, where a client that already carries an address brings it along.

An `inboundIds` entry that names no existing inbound rejects the whole call before anything is written. Past that, the inbounds are applied concurrently and independently: one that fails no longer stops the others, so a `success:false` response can still have created the client on the rest. Every error names the inbound it came from (`inbound 7: <message>`), and several failures are reported together, one per line. `limitHwid` is applied only when every inbound succeeded, so re-run the call after fixing the failure.

Protocol-specific: secret and adTag (mtproto), privateKey, publicKey, preSharedKey, allowedIPs and keepAlive (WireGuard).

Existing resetDay takes precedence over reset. With expiryTime=0, calendar modes suggest a first cutoff but do not activate renewal. Negative expiryTime waits for first-use activation. resetMax and resetCount simulate the existing per-period allowance limit; the preview is informational and does not reserve an allowance or guarantee node availability.

The inbounds are applied concurrently and independently: one that fails no longer stops the others. Every inbound error names the inbound it came from (`inbound 7: <message>`), and several failures are reported together, one per line. So a `success:false` response can still have applied the edit to the remaining inbounds. The client record is written after the inbounds, so a failure there is reported without an `inbound <id>:` prefix and leaves the inbound edits in place.

post.summary: Replace a client's external links and external subscriptions. Sends the full set; the server replaces all rows. Disabled rows stay saved for editing but are not emitted in generated subscriptions. The owning client's disabled or expired state also stops these rows from being emitted on future subscription fetches; credentials already imported by an app remain valid until the external provider revokes them.

externalLinks.description: Full replacement list; the server replaces all rows. Each row supports { kind, value, remark, enable, expiryTime, namePrefix }. kind=link: value must be a supported share link such as vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria2://, or wireguard://, and remark overrides the exported node name. kind=subscription: value must be an http(s) subscription URL, and namePrefix is prepended to fetched node names. Omit enable to default true; enable=false or an expired expiryTime keeps the row saved but excludes it from generated subscriptions. expiryTime is a unix millisecond timestamp where 0 means no link-specific expiry; the owning client's enabled state and expiry still apply. A negative value is rejected. Rows are matched by kind+value across saves, so id is ignored on write. lastFetchAt and lastFetchError are read-only status fields returned by GET.

Clients with no inbound attachment are included with an empty inboundIds list. The UI shows this in a CodeMirror viewer (copy / download); programmatic callers get the array in obj.

post.summary: Import clients from a JSON body { "data": "<json>" }, where data is a string-encoded array produced by /export ([{client, inboundIds, traffic}]). Items with inboundIds are created and attached to those inbounds; items with an empty inboundIds list are restored as unattached client records. An optional traffic object restores the usage counters, only for clients this import creates. Existing emails are never overwritten — they are returned in skipped, and their live counters are left untouched. Triggers a single Xray restart at the end if any target inbound was running; a failure while restoring counters still reports success=false after the clients were created.

Shift expiry and/or traffic quota for many clients in one call. addDays/addBytes may be negative. Clients with unlimited expiry (expiryTime=0) or unlimited traffic (totalGB=0) are skipped for the corresponding field — bulk extend never converts unlimited to limited. A client that was auto-disabled solely because it was depleted (expired or over quota) is automatically re-enabled — locally and on its node — when the adjustment lifts it out of depletion; a manually-disabled or still-depleted client is left disabled. The optional flow directive sets the XTLS flow on every client: "none" clears it, "xtls-rprx-vision"/"xtls-rprx-vision-udp443" set it where the inbound supports it (omit or "" to leave it unchanged). The optional limitHwid sets maximum registered devices (0 = unlimited); the optional speedLimit, limitIp and userLimit set that limit to the same value on every client. The optional adTag sets MTProto Telegram sponsor channel ("none" clears). Returns the adjusted count and per-email skip reasons.

Enable many clients in one call. Emails are grouped by inbound and applied with a single read-modify-write per inbound; the running Xray (local or remote node) is updated to add each user. Note that enabling a client whose quota is exhausted or whose expiry has passed only flips the flag — the traffic loop will disable it again on the next tick. Returns the changed count and per-email skip reasons.

Disable many clients in one call. Emails are grouped by inbound and applied with a single read-modify-write per inbound; the running Xray (local or remote node) is updated to remove each user. Returns the changed count and per-email skip reasons.

Delete many clients in one call. The server processes the list sequentially so each delete sees the committed state of the previous one — avoids the race the per-email fan-out had on the panel side. Pass keepTraffic=true to retain the xray_client_traffic rows after deletion.

Create many clients in one call. Body is a JSON array of {client, inboundIds} payloads — the same shape /add accepts. Items are processed sequentially; per-email skip reasons are returned for items that fail (e.g., duplicate email). Triggers a single Xray restart at the end if any inbound was running.

Add many clients to a group in one call. Updates clients.group_name and patches the matching client entry inside every owning inbound's settings JSON in a single transaction. If the group name does not yet exist (in client_groups or as a derived label), it is auto-created as a persistent group. To clear the group label, use /groups/bulkRemove instead.

Clear the group label on many clients in one call. Inverse of /groups/bulkAdd. Clients themselves are kept — only the group label is cleared from clients.group_name and from each owning inbound's settings JSON. Groups become empty if all their members are removed.

Attach many existing clients to many inbounds in one call. Each client keeps its identity (email/UUID/password/subId) and a shared traffic row; all clients are added to a target inbound in a single AddInboundClient call. Clients already present on a target are reported under skipped. Returns per-email attached/skipped/errors lists and triggers a single Xray restart if any target inbound was running.

post.summary: Reset traffic counters for a specific outbound by tag.
Test an outbound configuration. Sends the outbound JSON (required), optionally all outbounds (to resolve sockopt.dialerProxy dependencies), and a mode flag.

allOutbounds.description: JSON array of all outbounds — used to resolve dialerProxy chains.

mode.description: "tcp" for a fast dial-only probe (parallel-safe), "real" for a real-delay probe whose delay is the full request time including tunnel establishment. Default/empty uses a full HTTP probe reporting the warm per-request round-trip. Both HTTP variants run through a temp xray instance.

post.summary: Test a batch of outbounds (max 50) through one shared temp xray instance. Returns an array of results in input order, each with the outbound tag, delay, HTTP status and a connect/TLS/TTFB timing breakdown.

outbounds.description: JSON array of outbound configs to test (required).

allOutbounds.description: JSON array of all outbounds — used to resolve dialerProxy chains.

mode.description: "tcp" for fast dial-only probes (UDP-transport outbounds are still probed over HTTP), "real" for real-delay probes whose delay is the full request time including tunnel establishment. Default/empty routes an HTTP request through each outbound and reports the warm per-request round-trip.

post.summary: Live state of routing balancers in the running core (RoutingService.GetBalancerInfo): current override and the targets the strategy prefers. Returns a map keyed by balancer tag.

tags.description: Comma-separated balancer tags to query (e.g. "b1,b2").

post.summary: Force a balancer in the running core to always pick one outbound (RoutingService.OverrideBalancerTarget). Applied live without a restart and kept across config saves; cleared when Xray restarts or the target outbound is removed.

target.description: Outbound tag to force; it must exist in the running config. Empty clears the override and returns control to the strategy.

post.summary: Ask the running core which outbound its router would pick for a synthetic connection (RoutingService.TestRoute). No traffic is sent.

domain.description: Target domain. Either domain or ip is required.

ip.description: Target IP. Either domain or ip is required.

protocol.description: Sniffed protocol such as http, tls, bittorrent (optional).

get.summary: List the geo databases (.dat files) in the Xray asset folder, with the layout detected from their contents, size, modification time and category count. A database that fails to parse is still listed, with the reason in "error".
One page of a database's categories, each with its entry count and the attributes its domains carry (e.g. "ads", "cn").

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Database file name inside the asset folder, e.g. geosite.dat (required).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the category code.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows to return, capped at 500. Omit it to return every category — the index is small and the panel filters it client-side.

get.summary: One page of the rules inside a category — domain rules typed as domain/full/keyword/regexp for geosite databases, CIDRs for geoip ones.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Database file name inside the asset folder (required).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the rule value.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows to return, capped at 500. Defaults to the cap.

post.summary: Check routing tokens against the databases on disk and return only the ones that do not resolve. Plain domains and CIDRs are ignored. Each issue carries a reason: syntax, fileMissing or categoryMissing.

tokens.description: Comma-separated routing tokens, e.g. "geosite:google,geosite:blabla". Max 500 per request.

kind.description: "ip" to parse the tokens as IP rules (geoip:, ext-ip:, leading !). Anything else parses them as domain rules (geosite:, ext-site:).

get.summary: List all outbound subscriptions (remote URLs that supply additional outbounds), newest first.

post.summary: Create an outbound subscription. The URL is fetched, parsed into outbounds with stable tags, and merged additively into the running Xray config.

url.description: Subscription URL (required). Must be a public http(s) address; private/internal targets are blocked unless allowPrivate is true.

tagPrefix.description: Prefix for generated outbound tags. Defaults to the lowest free "sub<N>-" prefix.

userAgent.description: Custom User-Agent sent when fetching this subscription. Defaults to "manifold-outbound-sub/1.0".

enabled.description: Whether the subscription is active. Default true.

allowPrivate.description: Allow the URL to point at a private/internal/loopback address. Default false.

allowInsecure.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when fetching the subscription's URL. Default false.

prepend.description: Place this subscription's outbounds before the manual template outbounds. Default false.

post.summary: Update an existing outbound subscription by id. Accepts the same form fields as create.

dir.description: "up" to raise priority, anything else to lower it.

userAgent.description: Custom User-Agent sent while fetching the preview.

allowPrivate.description: Allow a private/internal/loopback URL. Default false.

get.summary: List all subscription balancers in sort order (sort_order asc, id asc).

post.summary: Create a subscription balancer. It appears in the JSON subscription of every client that sits on at least one selected inbound.

remark.description: Display label, used as the config remarks (required).

inboundIds.description: Repeated form keys selecting the member inbounds (required, at least one).

memberWeights.description: leastLoad only: JSON object mapping inbound id to a static weight > 0, e.g. {"3":0.2}. Lower weight = picked more often; absent ids weigh 1. Rejected for other strategies; entries for unselected inbounds are dropped.

sortOrder.description: 1-based position in the subscription list. Default 1.

enabled.description: Whether the balancer is emitted. Default true on create; unchanged when omitted on update.

post.summary: Update a balancer by id. Accepts the same form fields as create (full-row update); omitting memberWeights clears stored weights, while omitting enabled keeps its current value.

get.summary: List the locations, each with the ids of the inbounds that serve it.

post.summary: Create a location (id 0 or absent) or replace one, its inbounds included. Refused when the name is empty, the country is not a two-letter ISO 3166 code, the timezone is unknown, an inbound does not exist or already serves another location.
Delete a location. Its inbounds stay, serving no location.

get.summary: Return base64-encoded subscription links for all enabled clients matching the subscription ID. When the request has an Accept: text/html header or ?html=1, renders a styled info page instead. With ?format=info, returns the page view-model as JSON (traffic, expiry, online status; no links) for live polling. The path prefix is configured by subPath.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to "info" to get the subscription status view-model as JSON instead of the links.

head.summary: Return the same status and subscription metadata headers as GET without a response body.

200.description: Subscription is available. Headers match GET; no response body.

404.description: No enabled client matches the subscription ID.

get.summary: Return aggregate HWID device-slot usage for the subscription: whether an HWID limit is active, the limit, how many devices are registered and how many slots remain. Read-only — it never registers a device, so asking does not consume a slot. Counters only: no HWID value, email or device metadata. The path prefix is configured by subPath.
get.description: Responds with the bare HwidSlotStatus object, not the {success,msg,obj} panel envelope, like the other subscription-server routes. With no HWID limit configured, active is false and every counter is 0.

404.description: No enabled client matches the subscription ID. Empty body.

head.summary: Return the HWID device-slot status code and headers as GET without a response body.

200.description: Headers match GET; no response body.

404.description: No enabled client matches the subscription ID. Empty body.

post.summary: Sign a device in to the app with its subscription link and the username of one of the link's accounts. The device takes a slot of the same HWID limit the link's other apps share. Answers {"token":"..."}; the same app/v1 routes answer under every subscription path.
post.description: JSON body: username, deviceId (6-128 characters, stable per device), deviceName, os, osVersion, appVersion. Errors are {"error":code}: 403 app_disabled, 401 bad_login, 400 bad_device, 403 device_limit, 429 too_many_attempts (5 failures per address and link in 5 minutes block for 15).

get.summary: Return the signed-in account, its locations and every entry of its subscription, with the Xray outbound of each entry Xray can run. Needs Authorization: Bearer token and X-HWID: deviceId.
get.description: A session ends when the device is removed from the client's devices, the link is rotated, the account is renamed or app access is switched off; the call then answers 401 bad_session or 403 app_disabled, and 403 device_limit when the device lost its slot.

post.summary: End the session of the bearer token.

get.summary: Return subscription as a JSON array of proxy configs (one per enabled client). Only when JSON subscription is enabled in settings. The path prefix is configured by subJsonPath.

head.summary: Return the JSON subscription status and metadata headers without a body. Registered only when JSON subscriptions are enabled.

200.description: Subscription is available. Headers match GET; no response body.

404.description: No enabled client matches the subscription ID.

get.summary: Return subscription as a Clash/Mihomo-compatible YAML config, including configured global Clash routing rules. Only when Clash subscription is enabled in settings. The path prefix is configured by subClashPath.

head.summary: Return the Clash subscription status and metadata headers without a body. Registered only when Clash subscriptions are enabled.

200.description: Subscription is available. Headers match GET; no response body.

404.description: No enabled client matches the subscription ID.
